definition: Which way an assembly runs. Most rise up the wall, bottom to top, so each member's figure is a height; a casing runs across its face from the jamb outward, so its figures are widths. The pack states it; nothing guesses it.
basis: Our wording of the pack schema's axis field and the classical trim family's casing member notes. schema/proportion-pack.schema.json, axis description: "Which way the assembly runs, stated on the assembly rather than left in a member's note."; schema/proportion-pack.schema.json, axis description: "up-the-wall: the members stack bottom to top, as an order and a wall section do"; proportions/systems/trim-classical.json assemblies.casing_georgian.members[geo_cas_reveal].note: "This assembly is measured ACROSS the casing from the jamb outward rather than vertically; height_parts is therefore a width.".
